header.name: Linear Algebraic Group
header.description: Students who meet the mandatory prerequisites may opt for this course either for credit or audit purposes. The subject Linear Algebraic Group (LAG) lies at the intersection of Algebra, Geometry, and Representation theory. It is an algebraic geometric counterpart to the analytic theory of Lie groups. A linear algebraic group is a subgroup of invertible matrices, i.e. GL(n), and is defined by polynomial equations. Much of the theory of LAG was developed by analogy with Lie Groups. Yet the algebraic framework is far richer because it studies GL(n) over any field, even for positive characteristic. The goal of this course is to introduce the foundational concept and the construction of linear algebraic groups, and illustrate how they connect to Geometry and Representation Theory. The final aim is to understand the classification of semisimple linear algebraic groups.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Identify and describe some of the classical linear algebraic groups. Understand popular groups such as nilpotent, unipotent, semi-simple, and solvable in this subject.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Develop the topological and geometrical structure of linear algebraic groups.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Determine Lie Algebra of an algebraic group and classify semisimple linear algebraic groups.
